name: sol_basics_al_4
description: Using delete on an array element to remove an item, leaving a stale/zero placeholder instead of shrinking the array
question: The source file in `source` removes an item from an array by calling delete on that array's element (e.g. `delete arr[i]`) to eliminate it, without swapping the last element into that index and popping/decrementing the array length or otherwise removing the gap, so the array retains a stale zero-valued or default-valued placeholder entry at that index and its length is unchanged, leading to incorrect iteration, counting, or lookups over that array.
criteria: A function removes a user or item from an array via `delete arr[i]` and returns without reordering elements or calling pop(), leaving array length unchanged and a zero-valued gap at index i
A function sets `arr[index] = 0` or `arr[index] = address(0)` to 'remove' an entry from a tracking array but never reduces the array's length or fills the gap with the last element

Loop-based removal deletes an element in place (e.g. `delete list[found]`) instead of copying the last element into `found` and calling `list.pop()`, so subsequent code iterating over `list` still processes the deleted slot
